links.outcome: Model uncertainty (perplexity) with vs without PubMed evidence augmentation
links.effect: Evidence augmentation reduced uncertainty (perplexity 4.13) compared to base responses; full system 87% accuracy, relevance around 0.80.
links.quote: In evaluation, the full system achieves 87% accuracy with relevance around 0.80, and evidence augmentation reduces uncertainty (perplexity 4.13) compared to base responses, with mean end-to-end latency of 36.5 seconds under the reported configuration.

screen.reason: The paper empirically evaluates a multi-agent framework incorporating evidence retrieval grounding, uncertainty estimation, and bias filtering safeguards on a clinical QA benchmark dataset.
